status_model.notes: Integrity review and release readiness are independent dimensions. Schema validation or machine verification never changes review_state to approved.

coverage_policy.core_all_language_invariant: Every canonical vocabulary/concept required by a lesson part must have a resolvable lexicon realization or an explicit researched no-direct-equivalent record for every language in the canonical learn-from language program before that part may claim all-language Core coverage.
coverage_policy.tier3_core_policy: Tier 3 targets may provide Core comparison, recognition-safe games, reader quests, and annotated-reading discovery when the required concept coverage exists. This does not make them full grammar-learning targets.
coverage_policy.full_grammar_policy: Full grammar instruction is limited by the canonical language-support registry. At the current registry contract that means Tier 1 and selectively Tier 2, never Tier 3 merely because Core exists.

component_catalog.notes: Core cannot claim all-language coverage until every required concept resolves across the canonical learn-from program.
Core may use recognition-safe games even when production grammar practice is unavailable.
Corpus-side annotations live in gef-content and point back to lexicon concepts/lesson parts.

readiness_resolution.notes: Resolve each directional source-language to target-language view at read time. Exact pair overrides win. A dashboard may aggregate the resolved matrix, but generated summary rows are cache/projection data, never lesson truth. Any required component omitted from a readiness profile resolves as missing unless a more-specific override supplies it.
